title_zh: 能源、电力与基础设施走向融合 | Cohen & Steers Tyler Rosenlicht、VistaShares Adam Padey
subtitle_zh: 新通胀机制下，油气、电力与 AI 基础设施加速融合，两位嘉宾解读自然资源与主题 ETF 如何构建组合。
summary_zh: 本期 ETF Edge 由 Dominic Chu 主持，对话 Cohen & Steers 自然资源股票主管 Tyler Rosenlicht 与 VistaShares CEO Adam Padey，主题是能源、电力与基础设施在 AI 驱动下的加速融合。Rosenlicht 认为市场正处在一个新的通胀机制（inflation regime）中——未来通胀更高、更难预测，传统 60/40 股债组合的分散化效果下降，因此组合必须配置通胀敏感的实物资产（real assets）；中东局势与油价只是更大周期的一部分。他主张用自然资源股票而非商品期货来获取通胀贝塔（inflation beta）：股票能提供股息、由专业团队做商品决策、更好地在周期中复利，并规避期货的高持有成本与近月合约、升贴水（contango/backwardation）摩擦。Padey 补充油气真正的故事在柴油（由俄乌局势驱动、持续上行）以及粮食、水等战争时期的供给约束。两人详解 VistaShares 的方法论：跟着资本开支（CAPEX）走，用物料清单（bill of materials）识别供应链每一层的经济价值，旗下 AIS（AI 基础设施）、POW（电力）、GALX（太空）、R2（机器人）、AMMO（国防）等主题 ETF 由“实操者+组合构建人员”共同把关；节目还谈到主动管理 alpha 与不封顶的缓冲型（buffer）产品。是一堂关于自然资源与主题 ETF 如何构建抗通胀组合的实务课。

turns.en: BETF EDGE podcast is sponsored by Invesco QQQ. Let's rethink possibility. Invesco Distributors, Inc. Welcome to ETF EDGE, the podcast. If you're looking to learn the latest insights on all things exchange traded funds, you're in the right place. Every week, we're bringing you compelling interviews, thoughtful market analysis, and breaking down what it all means for investors.
turns.zh: 《ETF Edge》播客由 Invesco QQQ 赞助——Let's rethink possibility（重构无限可能）。Invesco Distributors, Inc. 欢迎收听《ETF Edge》播客。如果你想了解所有与 ETF（交易所交易基金）有关的最新洞见，你来对地方了。每周我们都会带来精彩的访谈、用心的市场分析，并为大家解读这一切对投资者意味着什么。

turns.en: I'm your host, Dominic Chu. Forget just oil volatility. There's a bigger upheaval at play as energy and power and infrastructure rapidly converge. Here's my conversation with Tyler Rosenlicht, Cohen and Sears, head of Natural Resource Equities, along with Adam Paddy, the CEO of VistaShares. Gentlemen, thank you very much for being here right now.
turns.zh: 我是主持人 Dominic Chu。别只盯着油价波动了——随着能源、电力与基础设施快速融合，一场更大的变局正在上演。下面是我与 Cohen & Steers 自然资源股票主管 Tyler Rosenlicht、以及 VistaShares CEO Adam Padey 的对谈。两位，非常感谢你们来到节目。

turns.en: I laid it out as an oil and gas trade only because oil and gas is garnering all the headlines these days, and it's mostly around what's happening with the Iran War. But maybe I'll go to you, Tyler, for this one first. When it comes to natural resource investing, when it comes to stuff that we dig out of the ground, is oil and gas vis-a-vis Iran the main driver behind some of the interest these days? And if so, can it last? It's a great question, and the reality for us is
turns.zh: 我把这期定位为油气交易，只是因为这些天油气抢尽了头条，而且大多与伊朗战争有关。这个问题我想先请教 Tyler：谈到自然资源投资，谈到我们从地下挖出来的东西，围绕伊朗的油气是不是最近这股兴趣的主要推手？如果是，它能持续吗？——这是个很好的问题。而对我们来说，现实是——

turns.en: it's way bigger picture than that. Obviously, what's going on in the Middle East today is really driving supply demand and balances for oil specifically and rising oil prices. But you have to look at the bigger picture cycle. For us, we think we're in a new inflation regime.
turns.zh: 这比那个图景大得多。显然，今天中东发生的事确实在驱动石油的供需平衡、推高油价。但你必须看更大的周期。对我们来说，我们认为自己正处在一个新的通胀机制（inflation regime）里。

turns.en: Inflation is going to be a lot higher on average and a lot less predictable going forward. Your traditional 60-40 stock bond portfolio from the last 20 years is no longer going to give you the same level of diversification and portfolio benefits. So for us, it's really about real assets broadly. It's about this idea that you need to have inflation sensitive in the portfolio. That's because supply of goods and supply of natural resources is constrained as the demand is accelerating.
turns.zh: 未来通胀的平均水平会高得多，也更难预测。过去二十年那种传统的 60/40 股债组合，不会再给你同样的分散化效果和组合收益。所以对我们而言，关键是广义的实物资产（real assets），是'组合里必须配置通胀敏感资产'这个理念。因为商品和自然资源的供给受限，而需求在加速。

turns.en: So we think oil is obviously sort of like very important, but it's not the only thing. It's part of like a much bigger, broader regime change that's underway.
turns.zh: 所以我们认为石油显然非常重要，但它不是唯一的东西。它是正在展开的更大、更广的机制转换的一部分。

turns.en: Adam, does that kind of maybe reconcile with what you're seeing from a thematic standpoint? Your firm, VistaShares, does a lot of thematic investing. You roll out a lot of thematic type ETFs on the actively managed side of things. How much do investors still have to pay attention to oil and gas, natural resources in general? How much of that is going to be more of a longer-term inflation hedge story? Not necessarily because you believe in oil and gas, per se, but just because
turns.zh: Adam，这和你在主题投资端看到的能对上吗？VistaShares 做了很多主题投资，在主动管理一侧推出了很多主题型 ETF。投资者在多大程度上仍需关注油气和一般自然资源？其中有多少会更像一个更长期的通胀对冲故事——不一定因为你本身相信油气，而只是因为——

turns.en: those types of products tend to be good hedges against an inflationary environment in the future. Well, I agree with, I agree with Tyler. I mean, bonds just aren't the hedge they used to be, right? I mean, in an inflationary environment, yields are going up. So the problem with oil and gas, it's really about the volatility, not about the direction, right? It's so headline-driven right now. I mean, if there's a peace deal where it's going to go down $10 a barrel, if there's
turns.zh: ——这类产品往往是对未来通胀环境的良好对冲。我同意，我同意 Tyler 的看法。债券已经不再是过去的对冲工具了，对吧？通胀环境里收益率在上升。而油气的问题，真正在于波动性，不在于方向。它现在太被头条驱动了。我是说，如果有和平协议，油价会一桶跌 10 美元；如果有升级——

turns.en: escalation, it's going to go back up $10 a barrel. I think the bigger story in kind of the broad oil and gas sector is really diesel, and that's being driven what's going on in Ukraine and Russia because diesel is what really drives industry and is really the inflationary, provides the inflationary pressure on all goods and services because all of our truck gang and so forth uses diesel. And that's where we're seeing the prices really sustain much higher levels.
turns.zh: ——局势升级，又会一桶涨回 10 美元。我认为更广泛的油气板块里，更大的故事其实是柴油，它是由乌克兰和俄罗斯的局势驱动的。因为柴油才是真正驱动工业的东西，它对所有商品和服务构成通胀压力——我们所有的卡车运输等等都烧柴油。我们看到的正是价格在真正维持在远高于过去的水平。

turns.en: And while they are volatile, not quite as volatile as the oil and gas, which is more consumer-driven, and diesel just keeps going up, right? It's not seeing those spikes down, it just keeps going up.
turns.zh: 而且柴油虽然有波动，但不像更偏消费驱动的油气那么剧烈，对吧？柴油就是一直在涨。它没有出现那种向下的尖峰，就是一直往上。

turns.en: In terms of overall natural resources, yeah, I mean, look, again, going back to Ukraine, look what's happened with there. They used to be the red basket of Europe, and now they can't get grain produced and sold. So food is a big issue, water is a big issue. I think we have issues across all the natural resources, particularly in times of war where it's harder to produce and ship than in days past. Tyler, how much do you then focus a little bit more away from the
turns.zh: 说到整体自然资源，是啊——我是说，还是回到乌克兰，看看那里发生了什么。他们过去是欧洲的粮仓，现在粮食没法生产、没法销售。所以食品是大问题，水也是大问题。我认为所有自然资源都有问题，尤其在战争时期，生产和运输都比过去更难。Tyler，那么你们在多大程度上更多地把重心从——

turns.en: traditional kind of oil and gas plays on price using those as a hedge? I mean, some people actually use exchange-traded products tied to things like the energy sector as a way to even hedge themselves at the pump, right? Because these oil and gas companies tend to go higher in price, as we see gasoline prices and oil prices go up as well. When you focus on those types of products and those types of, I guess, investing strategies, how much are investors
turns.zh: ——传统的油气标的移开，用它们来做对冲？我是说，有些人实际上把挂钩能源板块的交易所交易产品当作在加油站层面的对冲工具，因为这些油气公司的股价往往随着汽油和原油价格的上涨而上涨。当你聚焦这类产品、这类——姑且称之为投资策略——时，投资者在多大程度上正转向——

turns.en: turning a little bit more towards some of these exchange-traded products like ETFs around natural resources and energy as a way to actually take that kind of a view to hedge out inflationary risks.
turns.zh: ——自然资源和能源方面的这些交易所交易产品，比如 ETF，以此表达这种观点、对冲通胀风险？

turns.en: Yeah, I think it's really starting to pick up. It feels very early stage in terms of the recognition of where we are in the cycle and the need to have some of these things in your portfolio. But as people think about natural resource equities, which are obviously the companies that facilitate the extraction and the processing and the transportation of the resource economy versus commodity futures, for instance, we actually think natural resource equities are a really good way
turns.zh: 我觉得这股兴趣确实在升温。就大家对当前处于周期什么位置的认识、以及组合里需要配置这些资产的需求而言，现在感觉还非常早期。但当人们想到自然资源股票——显然是那些促成资源的开采、加工和运输的公司，而不是商品期货之类——我们实际上认为自然资源股票是获得——

turns.en: to get the portfolio benefits that you just talked about. You can get a dividend. You're investing in professional management teams that are helping you make the buy-sell commodity decision itself. You can compound the equity value in the commodity cycle a lot better via, we think, the equities than commodity futures. Commodity futures are expensive to maintain.
turns.zh: ——你刚才说的那些组合好处的一种很好的方式。你能拿到股息。你投资的是专业管理团队，他们在帮你做出商品买卖决策本身。相比商品期货，我们认为通过股票能在商品周期中更好地实现复利。商品期货的持有成本很高。

turns.en: You're very much as dependent on what's happening in the front month, not necessarily in the longer term. I'd say investors are starting to wake up to it. We think resource equities are a really good way to get real return hedging and very good inflation beta without some of the friction that you get with commodity futures products, as an example.
turns.zh: 你非常受制于近月合约（front month）的情况，而不是长期。我想说投资者正在开始觉醒。我们认为资源股票是获得实际回报对冲、获得很好的通胀贝塔（inflation beta）的好方式，同时规避商品期货类产品的那些摩擦成本，举个例子就是这样。

turns.en: Now, if I could follow up there, Tyler, if you can use those equities because they have more leverage over the commodity prices, they tend to move to a greater degree than some of the underlying actual commodities that they're involved with. For that reason, I wonder if you can take us through the reasons why we are seeing more of a focus on some of the other parts of the natural resource spectrum of products and commodities out there versus straight oil and gas. A lot of that
turns.zh: Tyler，我想接着问——既然可以用股票，因为它们对商品价格有更高的杠杆，股价波动往往比它们涉及的底层实际商品更大。正因如此，我想知道你能不能带我们梳理一下，为什么我们看到关注点正从单纯的油气转向自然资源和商品谱系里的其他部分。这在很大程度上——

turns.en: is because there is this whole narrative in the marketplace about trying to power the future, not the lease of which is being AI driven. Yeah, don't get me wrong. We really like traditional energy. We like oil and gas. I'd be happy to make the case for why we think multiples for traditional oil and gas companies like the oil sands need to go up a lot. But the reality is you could have an environment where inflation is picking up quite a lot, but maybe oil prices come
turns.zh: ——是因为市场上存在'为未来供电'（power the future）的整个叙事，其中尤以 AI 驱动。别误会，我们真的很喜欢传统能源，喜欢油气。我很乐意论证为什么我们认为油砂这类传统油气公司的估值倍数需要大幅上行。但现实是，可能出现通胀上行很多、但油价回落——

turns.en: down. And so your goal is to get inflation sensitivity and protection and good returns from your natural resources. But if all you're doing is investing in oil companies, you might miss the bigger picture. And so for us, we think investors are looking more broadly.
turns.zh: ——的环境。所以，如果你的目标是从自然资源中获得通胀敏感性、保护和不错的回报，但你做的事情只是投油气公司，那你可能会错过更大的图景。所以我们认为投资者正在把眼光放得更宽。

turns.en: They're saying this is a big regime change. I don't necessarily want to be wrong and have oil prices go from 185 and have my oil stocks go down in the short term. I want to make sure that I'm capturing the ag economy. I'm capturing the resource economy, metals and mining, gold prices, oil, natural gas, uranium, all the other parts of the sort of resource businesses that we look at.
turns.zh: 他们在说这是一次重大的机制转换。我不一定想判断错——万一油价从 185 往下走、我的油气股短期下跌呢。我要确保抓住农业经济、资源经济、金属与矿业、黄金价格、石油、天然气、铀，以及我们所研究的资源生意的所有其他部分。

turns.en: And so for us, it's kind of like, if you very small picture are excited about oil prices and oil, you know, oil ETFs are going to be great. But if it's, hey, I see this bigger thing happening, and I want to make sure that the portfolio is well positioned for it, that's why the lens is getting getting broadened and why these broader, more diversified natural resources strategies are really starting to get a lot of investor attention. Adam, how much more are traders and
turns.zh: 所以对我们来说，有点像这样：如果你只看很小的图景、对油价和石油感到兴奋，那石油 ETF 会很棒。但如果你说'嘿，我看到更大的东西正在发生，我要确保组合为此配置到位'——这就是为什么视角正在变宽，为什么这些更宽、更多元的自然资源策略开始获得大量投资者关注。Adam，在这样的市场里，交易者和——

turns.en: investors in this kind of a market using ETFs and exchange traded products that are tied to these types of themes? How much more are they using them? And are they using them strategically to take maybe medium or longer term views on a certain type of cycle or theme playing out?
turns.zh: ——投资者在多大程度上更多地使用挂钩这类主题的 ETF 和交易所交易产品？他们到底多用了很多吗？他们是否在战略性地运用它们，以表达对某类周期或主题展开的中期或长期观点？

turns.en: And how much of it has become more tactically oriented? Those who have shorter firm hold these things because of these more tactical moves in commodities or the underlying equities tied to them. You know, we talked a little bit about just how much the equities kind of differ in terms of performance against the underlying commodities. So are we seeing a little bit more investor and trader interest on the tactical use of some of these exchange traded funds
turns.zh: 还有多少变得更偏战术性？那些持有时间更短的人，正因为商品或其相关股票的这些更多战术性变动而这么做。我们刚才聊了一点股票与底层商品在表现上的差异。所以我们看到的，是更多投资者和交易者对战术性使用这些交易所交易基金的兴趣——

turns.en: or taking longer term secular views on them? Well, I think it depends on the on the resource that we're talking about. And I mean, my favorite resource to be invested in for the long term is electricity. Electricity, we have an ETF POW that covers it. It's one of our most popular ETFs, particularly of late. You talk about inflation hedging, right? At the biggest bottleneck, you mentioned AI is electricity. And it's going to take trillions of dollars deployed
turns.zh: ——还是对它们形成更长期的趋势性观点？我觉得这取决于具体说的是哪种资源。要说我最喜欢长期投资的资源，那就是电力。我们有只覆盖电力的 ETF 叫 POW，是我们最受欢迎的 ETF 之一，尤其最近是这样。你说通胀对冲吧——你提到的最大瓶颈，对 AI 来说就是电力。仅仅升级我们的电网，就需要数万亿美元的投入——

turns.en: to just upgrade our grid, putting aside data centers just for consumer use and electric cars and heat pumps and things like that. So, you know, electricity prices are continually rising, demand is continually rising, and it's outpacing supply. And there's tremendous bottlenecks on the equipment required to improve the grid with transformers and distribution transmission, really being a problem right there. So I would view those as more long term strategic allocations
turns.zh: ——先不谈数据中心，光是居民用电、电动车、热泵之类。所以电价持续上涨，需求持续上涨，且跑在供给前面。改善电网所需的设备存在巨大瓶颈，变压器、配电和输电确实就是问题所在。所以我会把这些看作组合里更长期的战略性配置。

turns.en: to your portfolio. And that's how our investors are using POW. And then of course, as Tyler mentioned, you know, I agree, I think the equities are a better place for most investors. You know, most investors don't understand contango and backwardation and all the issues related to futures based products. So if you look at kind of oil futures ETFs, they are better for short term use and you'll see more trading activity there. And that's a better use for them because
turns.zh: 我们的投资者就是这样使用 POW 的。当然，正如 Tyler 所说，我同意——对大多数投资者来说，股票是更好的去处。大多数投资者不懂 contango（期货升水）和 backwardation（期货贴水），也不懂期货类产品的种种问题。如果你看石油期货 ETF，它们更适合短期使用，你会在那儿看到更多交易活动，那样用它们更合适。因为它们——

turns.en: they won't necessarily track the spot price of oil as you may expect in different regimes based on that contango and backwardation and how the futures role works. Tyler, it wasn't maybe that long ago when we used to talk about stories around some of these types of products and use energy, referring specifically more to the kind of oil and gas side of things, and then power more towards the kind of power generation, electrification, infrastructure side of things.
turns.zh: ——基于升贴水和期货展期（roll）机制，在不同环境下未必会像你可能预期的那样跟踪油价现货。Tyler，也许不久之前，我们聊这类产品的故事时，'能源（energy）'还更专指油气那一块，而'电力（power）'更多指向发电、电气化、基础设施那一侧。

turns.en: These days, it really feels as though the energy and the power trade have now converged because specifically around the stories around AI. Is that how you see things playing out as well right now that energy and power are becoming closer and closer to synonymous given what's happening with AI? I think they are. And I think it's because it's not just because of AI, it's because of reindustrialization, it's because of the digitalization of the global economy,
turns.zh: 如今，真的感觉能源交易和电力交易已经融合了，特别是围绕 AI 的那些故事。你也觉得事情正在这样展开吗——随着 AI 的发展，energy 和 power 正变得越来越同义？我觉得是的。而且我认为这不仅是因为 AI，还因为再工业化（reindustrialization），因为全球经济的数字化——

turns.en: it's because of electricity demand, power demand, data centers, clearly all of the above. I think what the market is waking up to, and we talked about this five years ago when we launched one of our strategies, which is the Kona Steers Future of Energy Strategy, which is it's an energy addition world, not an energy transition. Yes, alternatives are going to gain market share, but we really need more of everything. We think oil demand is going to rise for a while and then plateau,
turns.zh: ——因为电力需求、用电需求、数据中心，显然是所有这些因素叠加。我认为市场正在觉醒。我们五年前推出我们的一个策略时就谈过这一点——Cohen & Steers 的 Future of Energy（未来能源）策略——这是一个能源'加法'（energy addition）的世界，而不是能源转型（energy transition）的世界。没错，替代能源会赢得市场份额，但我们真的需要所有能源都更多。我们认为石油需求会先上升一段时间，然后进入平台期；

turns.en: natural gas demand is going to rise for a really long time. Alternative energy is going to accelerate even faster given everything that we're seeing. And really it is about creating the electrons, the electricity, the power needed for the global economy to run, be it moving data, powering homes, or moving airplanes across the world. And so for us, I think the world is waking up to the fact that energy is going to be very different five years from now than it was five years ago. Five
turns.zh: 天然气需求将在很长时间里持续上升。基于我们看到的一切，替代能源会加速得更快。说到底，这是要创造电子——全球经济运转所需的电力，无论它是传输数据、为家庭供电，还是让世界上的飞机飞起来。所以对我们来说，我认为世界正在认识到：五年后的能源将和五年前非常不同。五

turns.en: years ago, when you heard energy, you just thought exon, oil and gas, traditional resources. Now when you hear energy, hopefully you think still exon, but also natural gas pipeline companies, natural gas producers, uranium companies, nuclear generation, all the power stack utilities, it's this much broader world, and it's a very sensible convergence in our view.
turns.zh: ——年前，你一听到'能源'，想到的就是 Exxon、油气、传统资源。现在听到能源，希望你仍然会想到 Exxon，但也会想到天然气管道公司、天然气生产商、铀公司、核电、整个电力板块的公用事业公司——在我们看来，这是一个宽广得多的世界，也是非常合理的融合。

turns.en: Okay, let's follow up on that. So I'm going to stick with you, Tyler, on this. Because you basically have a role that centers around the equity side of the natural resource trade. Can you take us through, you mentioned a number of different kind of themes or sectors or industries that are in focus for you. What types of companies are coming through as being at the forefront of some of those more kind of sub-industry themes that go into this power generation AI infrastructure
turns.zh: 好，我们接着聊这个。我就继续盯着你问，Tyler。因为你的角色基本围绕自然资源交易的股票端。你能不能带我们梳理一下——你提到了很多目前受关注的主题、板块或行业——在未来几年这场发电、AI 基础设施的交易里，哪些类型的公司会在那些更细分的行业主题中冲在最前面？

turns.en: kind of trade, I guess, in the coming years? Yeah, so we have a couple of different sort of portfolios and strategies. We have an infrastructure ETF, which is CSIO. We have a natural resources one CSNR, and then the future of energy strategy.
turns.zh: ——我是说，这场交易？是的，我们有几种不同的组合和策略。我们有一只基础设施 ETF，代码 CSIO；一只自然资源 ETF，代码 CSNR；还有 Future of Energy 策略。

turns.en: And for us, it's all about finding the bottlenecks and investing where we think the bottlenecks are going to have duration. You know, when I think about the AI, the power trade, what we're sort of talking about here, some of the biggest bottlenecks are natural gas, right? It's really hard to build natural gas pipelines here in North America. If you have incumbent natural gas pipelines in the ground, those are suddenly going to be more valuable. You know, we think that those businesses are
turns.zh: 对我们来说，核心就是找到瓶颈，并投资于我们认为瓶颈会持续存在的地方。说到 AI、电力这笔交易，我们谈到的最大瓶颈之一其实是天然气，对吧？在北美建天然气管道真的很难。如果你已经有现成的天然气管道埋在地上，它们会突然变得更有价值。我们认为这些企业——

turns.en: moving further downstream. They're not just about moving natural gas molecules from supply basins to demand basins, but it's actually about getting power behind the meter at data centers.
turns.zh: ——正在进一步往下游走。它们不只是把天然气分子从供给盆地运到需求盆地，而是真正要在数据中心实现'表后'（behind-the-meter）供电。

turns.en: So that's a theme that we really like. You know, we really like the engineering and construction businesses that are building all the utility infrastructure. One of the tricky things with utilities right now is there's almost too much opportunity. And all that opportunity in CAPX is inflationary to the customers. And they're going to see some challenge returns potentially in a midterm election year. Actually, the companies that build the infrastructure for them, we think
turns.zh: 这是我们非常喜欢的主题。我们也很喜欢那些承建所有公用事业基础设施的工程与建设公司。现在公用事业公司有个棘手的问题：机会几乎多到过头，而所有这些资本开支（capex）对客户来说都是通胀性的，他们可能会看到一些颇具挑战的回报——又恰逢中期选举年。实际上，那些为他们建设基础设施的公司，我们认为——

turns.en: are going to see great opportunities because, hey, their demand is rising, their supply constraint in terms of skilled labor is getting harder and harder. So that's another one we like. Like I said, uranium, nuclear generation, it's clean, it's predictable, it's high capacity factors, low variability. It's the kind of energy the world wants. And so again, at the core, find the bottlenecks.
turns.zh: ——会看到极好的机会。因为需求在上升，而技能劳动力的供给约束越来越紧。所以这也是我们喜欢的一个方向。就像我说的，铀、核电——清洁、可预测、容量利用率（capacity factor）高、波动低。这是这个世界想要的能源。所以归根结底，核心还是找到瓶颈。

turns.en: Where is the bottleneck underappreciated and longer lasting? And we think there's great opportunities across infrastructure, natural resources and energy when you look with that kind of lens. Adam, how do you actually construct an underlying index or portfolio to track some of these kind of, I guess, more prevalent themes that are developing here? In other words, as you put a fund together, what exactly then goes into the fund? How exactly do you decide what goes into
turns.zh: 瓶颈在哪里被低估、且能持续更久？我们认为，用这种视角去看，基础设施、自然资源和能源里都有很好的机会。Adam，你们到底怎么构建一个底层指数或组合，去跟踪这些我猜正变得越来越主流、正在成形的主题？换句话说，当你组建一只基金时，到底是什么进了这只基金？你怎么决定什么进——

turns.en: a fund? And how exactly do you figure out what goes in and out? How do you rebalance? How do you tactically allocate? How exactly does a firm like VistaShares take some of these bigger kind of constructs and ideas around themes and turn them into an actual product that people use on an exchange-traded fund basis? We have a very novel approach. We actually develop what we call the bill of materials approach. And we file the patent on this. And
turns.zh: ——这只基金？你怎么决定什么进、什么出？怎么再平衡？怎么战术性配置？VistaShares 这样的公司，到底怎么把这些更大的主题构想和理念，变成大家在交易所交易基金层面实际使用的产品？我们有一种很新颖的方法。我们实际上开发了所谓的物料清单（bill of materials）方法，还为此申请了专利。

turns.en: what it is is very simple. We follow the CAPEX. So what we'll do is we'll, whether it's AI infrastructure or electrification, we have AIS for that, we have POW, we have robotics and other funds, we will first analyze the supply chain to identify all the different segments of the supply chain. Then we overlay the bill of materials. And what the bill of materials really does is really just identify the economic value of each level of the supply chain. So just taking AIS
turns.zh: 而它的原理很简单：我们跟着资本开支（CAPEX）走。无论是 AI 基础设施还是电气化——AI 基础设施我们有 AIS，电力有 POW，还有机器人和其他基金——我们会先分析供应链，识别供应链的所有不同环节，然后叠加上物料清单。物料清单真正做的，就是识别供应链每一层的经济价值。就拿 AIS——

turns.en: for instance, our AI infrastructure ETF, many people don't know that cooling systems are around 25% of overall CAPEX spend building a data center. So very important. So once we overlay the bill of materials, then we'll analyze the actual companies to see how much of their business is actually coming from electrification or AI infrastructure or robotics infrastructure business. Because taking cooling, for instance, we don't care about cooling companies. We don't even care about
turns.zh: ——我们的 AI 基础设施 ETF——来说，很多人不知道，制冷系统约占建设一个数据中心总资本开支的 25%，所以非常重要。叠加物料清单之后，我们再分析实际公司，看它们的业务中有多大比例真正来自电气化、AI 基础设施或机器人基础设施业务。因为就拿制冷来说，我们并不关心制冷公司。我们甚至不关心——

turns.en: cooling companies that are building data centers. We only care about cooling companies that are supplying their year for AI data centers. So you really got to tease out those financials to understand what their pipelines look like. And that builds the core of our portfolio.
turns.zh: ——建数据中心的制冷公司。我们只关心为 AI 数据中心供货的制冷公司。所以你真的得把财务数据一点点拆出来，理解它们的订单管线（pipeline）长什么样。而这就构成了我们组合的核心。

turns.en: So we're getting a full representation of what it actually takes to build these systems. So we like to say when somebody builds an AI data center, the cash register rings across AIS's entire portfolio. And that is consistent across POW, R2, Galaxy, all of our products.
turns.zh: 所以我们得到的是'建起这些系统到底需要什么'的完整代表性图景。我们喜欢说：当有人建一座 AI 数据中心时，AIS 整个组合的收银机都会响。这在 POW、R2、Galaxy 以及我们的所有产品中都是一致的。

turns.en: But the secret sauce is really identifying people to sit on the investment committee that are operators. So we're not doing just analysis. We actually pull people onto our investment committees that are experts in the space. So if you look at who we have, these are people who are building the companies, who are building the data centers, who are thought leaders in energy technology, who are actually, you know, understand the pipelines, understand the technologies and
turns.zh: 但真正的秘方，是找到坐在投资委员会里的实操型人才（operators）。我们不只是做分析。我们真的会把该领域的专家请进我们的投资委员会。你看看我们都有谁——这些人是在建公司的人、在建数据中心的人，是能源技术领域的思想领袖，他们真正懂管线、懂技术——

turns.en: understand the changes before the bottlenecks occur. And that's really our secret sauce, is really tapping into that expertise of the operators to choose companies or at least identify opportunities where we can find the companies to fulfill the new opportunities that they raise. Tyler, let's talk about whatever secret sauce you guys have. What exactly is passing your screening process right now from your portfolio managers through your investment
turns.zh: ——也懂瓶颈出现之前的那些变化。这才是我们真正的秘方：借助实操者的专业知识来选择公司，或者至少识别机会，找到能满足他们提出的新机会的公司。Tyler，聊聊你们的'秘方'吧。眼下从你们的组合经理、到投资——

turns.en: executives and your teams and analysts about the kinds of companies that will fill the portfolio around next-gen power and infrastructure? Are there specific names that are coming to the forefront? Which ones have kind of really passed your screens and are going to stick around? And which kinds of companies, perhaps, are the ones that you're maybe looking for to take a bigger role in your portfolios in the coming quarters and years? Yeah, absolutely. So, I mean, Cohen and
turns.zh: ——高管和团队、分析师，正在筛选什么样的公司来填充下一代电力和基础设施的组合？有没有具体的名字正冲在前面？哪些真的通过了你们的筛选、会留下来？哪些类型的公司，也许正是你们希望它们在未来几个季度和几年里在组合中扮演更大角色的？——是的，当然。我是说，Cohen &

turns.en: Steers, we only do a few things, but we try to do those things really well. You know, we are listed real assets, which is REITs, natural resource equities, infrastructure, energy, and then we have some alternative income as well. You know, we invest in those sectors because we think that there is the ability for active managers to add alpha. There's inefficiencies. So take infrastructure as an example. You know, the biggest challenge right now with infrastructure investment is
turns.zh: ——Steers 我们只做几件事，但我们努力把这些事做到极致。我们是上市实物资产（listed real assets）公司——REITs、自然资源股票、基础设施、能源，然后我们还做一些另类收益。我们投这些板块，是因为我们认为主动管理人能在这里创造 alpha（超额收益），这里有无效性。拿基础设施举例——现在基础设施投资最大的挑战是——

turns.en: regulatory risk and the rules getting changed. You think about investing in utilities. You know, utilities can see their returns benefit or hindered based on the decision of a few utility commissioners sitting in a room somewhere sort of deciding what they want to do for the local customers and ratepayers. So for us, it's about alpha for active management, and that can come from, hey, where do we find the best themes? You know, we want to make sure that we're investing
turns.zh: ——监管风险，以及规则被改来改去。你想想投公用事业：几位公用事业监管委员（utility commissioners）坐在某个房间里，决定为当地客户和缴费用户怎么做，公用事业的回报就可能因此受益或受损。所以对我们来说，核心是主动管理的 alpha，它可以来自——嘿，我们去哪找到最好的主题？我们想确保我们投资——

turns.en: obviously where the excitement is, where the growth is, and where the better opportunities are, and then identify the best relative value. So, hey, within data centers today, or sorry, within infrastructure today, we think some regions are inviting data center growth.
turns.zh: ——的地方显然是热度所在、增长所在、更好机会所在，然后识别最好的相对价值。所以，嘿——今天，在数据中心里，抱歉，在基础设施里——我们认为有些地区欢迎数据中心的增长。

turns.en: Some are going to constrain it. You know, in June, there were 92 local moratorium on data center development. Today, there's 520. So we want to find the places that are not putting up the moratorium that are actually inviting data centers into their service territory. And then we're trying to find the best relative value opportunity. So, hey, where is the growth underappreciated?
turns.zh: 有些地区则会限制它。六月的时候，有 92 项地方性数据中心开发禁令（moratorium）。到今天，已经有 520 项。所以我们想找到那些没有设禁令、真正欢迎数据中心进入其服务区域的地方。然后我们在寻找最好的相对价值机会：哪里的增长被低估？

turns.en: Where's the management team's ability to execute the best? It's utilities like Black Hills and Entergy. It's natural gas pipeline companies like Williams. So again, it's those theme identification within fundamental bottom-up work to find out where's the market mispricing the opportunity set, and where can we generate alpha by positioning accordingly.
turns.zh: 哪里的管理团队执行力最强？是 Black Hills、Entergy 这样的公用事业公司，是 Williams 这样的天然气管道公司。所以还是那句话：主题识别加上自下而上的基本面工作，找出市场对机会集在哪里定价错误、我们如何通过相应配置来创造 alpha。

turns.en: All right, so there's a handful of those names that we just went through here. Adam, for you, what types of names are coming through individually speaking? Are there certain types of companies or stocks that are featuring more prominently in some of the screening processes that you're doing? So if you look at electrification, for instance, and analyze where the CAPEX is being deployed, there's a lot of noise around the generation area, but it's only around 15% of
turns.zh: 好，刚才我们过了其中一些名字。Adam，对你来说，个股层面有哪些名字在冒出来？有没有某些类型的公司或股票在你们的筛选流程里更显眼？比如你看电气化（electrification），分析资本开支实际投向哪里——围绕发电环节噪音很大，但它只占总资本开支的大约 15%。

turns.en: total CAPEX. So where the CAPEX is actually being deployed is in distribution and transmission. So it's the boring, it's the switching equipment, it's the cabling. Believe it or not, it's the transformers. When you go outside and you look up on those big poles, those are transformers at the top. You can't get transformers. So it's the companies like Prismian. It's the companies like Eaton, Powell Industries, Delta Electronics that are providing kind of those nuts and bolts,
turns.zh: ——的资本开支。所以资本开支实际投向的是配电和输电。所以是那些'无聊'的东西：开关设备、电缆。信不信由你，还有变压器。你走到外面抬头看那些大电线杆，顶上那些就是变压器。变压器你根本买不到。所以是 Prysmian 这样的公司，是 Eaton、Powell Industries、Delta Electronics 这样的公司在提供这些'螺丝螺母'——

turns.en: and the backlogs they have for getting their equipment are sometimes a year or two long at this point. They can't produce enough, and that's what we're focused most of our allocations on these days. All right. So the energy trade, kind of morphing into the power trade, morphing into the infrastructure and electrification trade, all of these themes playing out at once here.
turns.zh: ——而它们拿设备的订单积压（backlog）如今有时长达一到两年。它们产量不够，这就是我们目前大部分配置聚焦的地方。好——能源交易变成电力交易，再变成基础设施与电气化交易，所有这些主题同时在展开。

turns.en: Now it's time to round out the conversation with some thoughtful analysis and perspective to help you better understand ETFs with our Markets102 portion of the podcast. Adam Paddy, this to share CEO continues with us now. Adam, we talked a lot about the natural resource theme that's been playing out and how there's a convergence, a blurring of the lines between the traditional energy trade, the traditional power trade, the electrification trade, and everything else coming together.
turns.zh: 现在，进入我们节目的 Markets102 环节，用一些用心的分析和视角帮你更好地理解 ETF。Adam Padey——VistaShares 的 CEO——继续和我们一起。Adam，我们刚才聊了很多正在展开的自然资源主题，聊传统能源交易、传统电力交易、电气化交易之间界限的模糊与融合——万物汇聚。

turns.en: That's indicative of many parts of the market that are seeing some transitions happening right now because of things like AI as a massive theme. I wonder as the CEO of an ETF provider, an issuer, how exactly do you come up with the themes you think will resonate the most with investors, because those that resonate tend to garner more assets, leading to a better profitability picture for you as an ETF issuer. So how do you strategically come up with the products you think will resonate
turns.zh: 这预示着市场的许多部分正因为 AI 这样的宏大主题而发生转型。我想知道，作为一家 ETF 发行商的 CEO，你到底是怎么想出你认为最能引起投资者共鸣的主题的？因为能引起共鸣的主题往往会吸来更多资产，对你这样的 ETF 发行商来说盈利图景就更好。所以你如何在战略上想出你认为最能引起共鸣的——

turns.en: the most with investors? Well, we're a little old fashioned. We talk to investors. We go out and we talk to investors all day long. We try to understand the pain points, what's missing in their portfolios, what they have and can be improved given new market environments. So on the thematic side, what we do is we tend to focus on what we view as super cycles. So these super cycles are technology driven trends that are decades in the making and decades long. So AI is certainly one of them.
turns.zh: ——产品？嗯，我们有点老派：我们跟投资者聊。我们整天在外面跟投资者交流。我们试图理解痛点、理解他们组合里缺什么、在新的市场环境下已有的东西怎么改进。所以在主题这一侧，我们专注于我们视为超级周期（super cycle）的东西。这些超级周期是由技术驱动的趋势，酝酿数十年、持续数十年。AI 当然是其中之一。

turns.en: Industrial revolution was a super cycle. The internet was a super cycle. So these are massive trends that develop that really change the way people live, work, and change economies completely.
turns.zh: 工业革命是一个超级周期。互联网是一个超级周期。所以，这些不断演进的、真正改变人们生活和工作方式、彻底改变经济的，是巨大的趋势。

turns.en: So AI, robotics, space, defense even at this point, right? The way milled technology has been changing and electrification. So we want to create foundational technology exposures that are meaningful for investors for the next decade or two. Similarly, we've been in a lot of volatility lately and investors are fearful and they're looking for novel ways to get downside protection, but still retain some upside potential. So the buffer space has really been important for investors
turns.zh: 所以——AI、机器人、太空，甚至到了今天的国防，对吧？军事技术一直在变——还有电气化。我们想创造的是对投资者未来一二十年有意义的基础性科技敞口。同样，我们最近经历了很多波动，投资者害怕，他们在寻找新颖的方式获得下行保护、同时保留一些上行潜力。所以缓冲型（buffer）空间对投资者真的很重要——

turns.en: for that purpose. The problem with many buffers is that they're year long or they're quarterly resets or you have to buy multiple products or a laddered product to get monthly exposure.
turns.zh: ——为了这个目的。而很多缓冲型产品的问题是：它们是一整年的，或是季度重置，要么你得买多个产品、或者买阶梯式（laddered）产品才能获得月度敞口。

turns.en: So what we did is we launched yesterday two brand new products, Ticker Vuby, VOOB, which covers the S&P 500 and QQQB, which is the NASDAQ 100. And we set out to solve all of the issues with buffers that investors have been complaining about, the serialization, the cliff risk on the downside of the buffer, the lack of upside. So what these are very simple, they are monthly rebounds products. They are designed to give you 8% hard buffer assistance to protect against
turns.zh: 所以我们昨天推出了两只全新产品：代码 VOOB，覆盖标普 500；QQQB，覆盖纳斯达克 100。我们着手解决投资者一直在抱怨的缓冲型产品的所有问题——期数化（serialization）、缓冲下限处的悬崖风险（cliff risk）、上行的缺失。这些产品很简单，它们是月度重置型产品，设计为给你 8% 的硬缓冲保护，去抵御——

turns.en: the first 8% and then below the 8% will absorb 50% of any downside as tail risk and every single month you get that same protection. And why that's important is it goes back to your first point is that things are so volatile right now. There's so much headline risk. The market can go up and down 5%, 3% a day just based on a tweet. And you need to have monthly protection to deal with that.
turns.zh: ——前 8% 的下跌，然后在 8% 以下作为尾部风险吸收任何下跌的 50%，每个月你都获得同样的保护。为什么这很重要？回到你说的第一点：现在波动太大，头条风险太多。市场可能光凭一条推文就一天上下 5%、3%。你需要每月都有的保护来应对。

turns.en: So it's a whole different environment which requires different solutions. That old school style of talking to investors to get an idea of what they're looking for, when you talked and spoke with investors about kind of the buffer space, because let's be honest, a lot of folks are out there putting buffer products out there to find outcome type products out there.
turns.zh: 所以这是一个完全不同的环境，需要不同的解决方案。说到那种与投资者交流以了解他们需求的老派方式——当你和投资者聊缓冲型产品空间时——因为说实话，现在很多人在那里推缓冲型产品、推结果型（outcome）产品。

turns.en: It is one of the fastest growing parts of the actively managed ETF ecosystem right now. When you spoke to those investors, investment advisors, retail traders and everybody else you spoke to to kind of get an idea of how you wanted to roll product out, what exactly was the feedback there? Was it that overwhelming where you felt as though they wanted that kind of defined outcome protection? And if so, why is it that
turns.zh: 这是当前主动管理 ETF 生态中增长最快的部分之一。当你和那些投资者、投资顾问、散户交易者以及所有你聊过的人交流，想了解你们打算怎么推出产品时，得到的反馈到底是什么？反馈是否强烈到让你觉得他们想要那种定义结果（defined outcome）的保护？如果是，那为什么——

turns.en: everybody is flooding into this space and how exactly do you stand out with your products given what you've got going on? I know that yours is different because you have a monthly kind of buffer reset, but these are all types of conversations that lead to different types of products coming out. How exactly did those conversations go for you to lead you to VOOB and QQQB? So we can't be everything to everybody. We're a small company,
turns.zh: ——所有人都在涌入这个领域？在你们已有布局的情况下，你们的产品到底怎么脱颖而出？我知道你们不一样，因为你们的缓冲是月度重置，但这些都是会导向不同类型产品的对话。那些对话到底是怎么进行的，让你做出了 VOOB 和 QQQB？——我们不可能面面俱到。我们是一家小公司——

turns.en: we're around 2.5 billion in assets. So growing fast, that's after 18 months. So I'm proud of that. But we were trying to develop products that are evergreen. So the problem with current buffers is that advisors need to ladder them. They need to roll in and out of different monthly series every month, and that's a lot of work for them. So the other providers have come up with laddered versions and things like that. Often their times are ETF of ETS or they're a
turns.zh: ——资产大约 25 亿美元。18 个月做到这个规模，增长很快，我为此自豪。但我们想做的是常青（evergreen）型产品。现有缓冲型产品的问题在于，顾问要把它们做成阶梯：每个月要滚动进出不同的月度期数，对他们来说是很大的工作量。其他发行商就搞出了阶梯式版本之类的东西，往往它们是 ETF 套 ETF（ETF of ETFs），或者有点——

turns.en: little clunky. So what we really just try to do is say, okay, if you can design something for downside protection, what would it be? It would be an evergreen product. They buy once, you set it and forget it. And then having 20% hard buffer is nice, but how often does the market actually go down 20%? Not often. Typically, the market grinds down over a series of months. So you need to have that protection reset every month. The market might go down five and up six and then down three and
turns.zh: ——笨重。所以我们真正想的是：如果让你为下行保护设计一个东西，它会是什么？那应该是一个常青产品——买一次，设好就不用管。20% 的硬缓冲当然不错，但市场多久才真的跌一次 20%？不常见。市场通常是在一连串月份里慢慢阴跌。所以你需要保护每个月重置。市场可能跌 5、涨 6，然后跌 3、

turns.en: down five. So we need to have that protection every single month. And what we found in our analysis is that 8% was the optimal range. The markets rarely go down below 8%, even in really distressful times. But to protect, you still want to have that tail risk insurance, right? So we're not going to give you 100% under the 8%, but we'll give you 50%. So if the market goes down 20, we protect against the eight, and then we split the 12. So we're down six, the market's down 20. But then the
turns.zh: ——再跌 5。所以我们需要每个月都有那个保护。我们的分析发现，8% 是最优区间。市场即使在最恐慌的时期也很少跌到 8% 以下。但为了保护自己，你还是想要那份尾部风险保险，对吧？所以我们不会在 8% 以下给你 100% 的保护，但会给你 50%。所以如果市场跌 20，我们保护前 8，然后剩下 12 我们分摊一半：我们跌 6，市场跌 20。但到了——

turns.en: next month, you get the full protection back. So it's just a very different structure. The other part of it is that most of the buffers out there, just by the way they do their option strategies, they're capping the upside. So they're good on the downside, bad on the upside. We did it without a cap. So you're still going to get only partial exposure to the upside just because that's what the nature of the product is. But it should give you a little more upside potential than the traditional
turns.zh: ——下个月，你又获得完整的保护。所以这是一个非常不同的结构。另一部分是，市面上大多数缓冲型产品，就凭它们做期权策略的方式，它们在给上行封顶——下行不错，上行很差。我们做成了不封顶的。因为产品性质使然，你仍然只有部分上行敞口，但它应该比传统——

turns.en: buffers, which we think is important. So it's good for investors that are looking for a hedge on their equity exposure. And frankly, it's really good for bond investors. You haven't gotten anything out of bonds in years. These are 2% to 4% volatility. You get more protection on the downside than with bonds. And you still get that bond or bond plus exposure for the upside.
turns.zh: ——缓冲型产品给你多一些上行潜力，我们认为这很重要。所以它适合那些想给股票敞口做对冲的投资者。坦白说，它对债券投资者也很好：这些年你从债券里什么都没拿到。这些产品波动率 2% 到 4%，下行保护比债券还多，上行你还能保留债券或'债券加'的敞口。

turns.en: All right. So you have basically index products that have derivative type strategies built around them to give you some of these more desired or defined outcomes. Can we also then talk about some of the other products that you have that are not necessarily broad index based, but still have to be constructed with portfolios of securities to then track a certain type of theme or industry group or some trend. You have a number of those products out as well. How exactly do you actively
turns.zh: 好。所以你们基本上是做指数型产品，围绕它们构建衍生型策略，给你一些更想要的、定义好的结果。那我们能不能也聊聊你们的另外一些产品——不一定基于宽基指数，但同样要用一篮子证券构建组合，去跟踪某种主题、行业组或某个趋势。你们也有不少这类产品。你们到底怎么主动——

turns.en: manage? How do you construct the underlying portfolios? And then how do you actively manage them so that they are giving investors kind of the best exposure that you can for the types of themes that they want to build into their own portfolios? Great question. And I've been in the ETF business since 2002. So I'm an old timer. But the ETF industry is notorious for creating portfolios and naming them something. And they're being a major mismatch. Calling something AI fund and you look
turns.zh: ——管理？怎么构建底层组合？然后怎么主动管理它们，使它们为投资者想在组合里构建的那类主题提供你能给出的最佳敞口？——好问题。我从 2002 年就进入 ETF 行业了，算是老江湖。但 ETF 行业有个臭名昭著的现象：先造一个组合、再贴个名字，两者严重错配。管自己叫 AI 基金，你打开——

turns.en: under the hood and you're like, what am I buying? It's just the nature of the business. It is what it is. And I wish I could take credit for this, but my partner, this gentleman named John McNeil, he was the president of Tesla. He's a brilliant businessman, brilliant technologist. And he was looking for exposure in the AI space, looked under the hood of a couple of the products, realized, wait a minute, these are not AI exposure. These are not AI companies. And so he said
turns.zh: ——引擎盖一看：'我买的到底是什么？'这就是这个行业的本性，事情就是如此。我真希望这能算我的功劳，但这来自我的合伙人，一位叫 John McNeil 的先生——他曾任特斯拉（Tesla）总裁——一位出色的商人、出色的技术专家。他当时想在 AI 领域找敞口，看了几只产品的'引擎盖下面'，意识到：等等，这些根本不是 AI 敞口，这些不是 AI 公司。于是他说——

turns.en: there's got to be a better way. And he actually developed this bill of materials process where we analyze the supply chain. So taking AI infrastructure for in instance, we have AIS, which is one of our leading products there. We'll analyze the supply chain. So every single component that goes into a data center or a semiconductor is analyzed and laid out onto a supply chain map. Then what we do is we overlay the bill of materials. So we'll say, okay, cooling is
turns.zh: ——一定有更好的办法。他实际开发了这套物料清单（bill of materials）流程，我们由此分析供应链。就拿 AI 基础设施来说——比如我们的领先产品之一 AIS——我们会分析供应链：进入一座数据中心或一颗半导体的每一个组件都被分析并铺在一张供应链地图上。然后我们叠加上物料清单。我们会说，好，制冷——

turns.en: every dollar that goes into a data center. Cooling is a dollar. Racking is 15 cents. And we'll just go down the list to see how important economically every level of the supply chain is. Once we understand that, then we'll start mapping companies to each level of the supply chain. And we'll start digging into their financials to understand, okay, this company is in cooling, but is it in AI data center cooling? Because that's what we want. We don't care about cooling
turns.zh: ——数据中心里投入的每一块钱中，制冷占一块钱，机架占 15 美分。我们就这么一层层列下去，看供应链每一层在经济上有多重要。理解了这个之后，我们再开始把公司映射到供应链的每一层，并深挖它们的财务数据，搞清楚：这家公司做制冷，但它做的是 AI 数据中心制冷吗？因为那才是我们要的。我们不关心制冷——

turns.en: companies. We want companies that are actually filling their own business pipeline with AI deals. So we'll do that analysis, and then we'll weight up, weight all those companies based on their contribution to their individual supply chain segments. And we'll roll that into a core portfolio.
turns.zh: ——公司。我们要的是真正用 AI 订单填满自身业务管线的公司。做完那套分析，我们就按各公司对各自供应链环节的贡献来给所有公司加权，并汇总成一个核心组合。

turns.en: And that's why we, so we're, you know, the portfolio is, it was all about identifying where the CAPEX is being deployed and who is making the money from that CAPEX. But then the secret sauce is really in the expertise on the investment committee. So our core portfolio looks very different than anyone else's core portfolio in the space, whether it's our, you know, R2, our robotics or GLX, our space or ammo or defense product, they all look very different.
turns.zh: 这就是为什么——这个组合的一切，是识别资本开支（CAPEX）投向哪里、谁从这些资本开支中赚钱。但真正的秘方在于投资委员会上的专业。所以我们的核心组合和这个领域里任何他人的核心组合都长得很不一样——无论是我们的 R2（机器人）、GLX（太空），还是 AMMO（国防）产品，它们都与众不同。

turns.en: But the secret sauce is the people who are identity or kind of overseeing the portfolio, because what we've tried to do is bring on a combination of operators and portfolio construction people. So the operators are the ones that are doing it every day, they're building data centers, they are out there creating new energy technologies. They are, you know, building spacecraft, you know, our space ETF, GALX, we have this gentleman named Ian Sineman, who's the CEO of
turns.zh: 但真正的秘方是那些识别机会、监督组合的人。因为我们试图把实操者（operators）和组合构建人员结合起来。实操者是每天在做这些事的人——建数据中心的、在外面创造新能源技术的、造航天器的。拿我们的太空 ETF GALX 来说，我们有位叫 Ian Sineman 的先生，他是——

turns.en: APEX Space. He's the leading provider of satellite buses. I mean, it's a wild industry. But those are the people that guide where the bottlenecks are, because they see the bottlenecks before anyone else does, because they're the ones who are building the products. So once they identify risks and opportunities in the portfolio, then it goes over to the portfolio construction people, which is more my side. And where we analyze the companies, we'll put it on a watch list
turns.zh: ——APEX Space 的 CEO，该公司是卫星平台（satellite bus）的领先供应商。我是说，这是个疯狂的行业。但正是这些人指引瓶颈在哪里，因为他们比任何人都先看到瓶颈——因为他们就是造产品的人。一旦他们识别出组合里的风险和机会，就转到组合构建人员这边，也就是更偏我这侧的工作。我们分析公司，把它们放上观察名单——

turns.en: and kind of see how it all plays out and then express the views of the operators into the portfolio. So it's just a different approach to portfolio construction and it's worked out quite well. AIS has, you know, been the top performing AI ETF in the world, POWA, I think is the top performing electrification ETF in the world right now. So, you know, performance comes and goes. It's no guarantees, but the supply chain, CAPEX, profit pool,
turns.zh: ——然后看这一切如何演变，再把实操者的观点表达进组合。所以这只是组合构建的一种不同方法，而且效果相当不错。AIS 一直是全球表现最好的 AI ETF；POW，我想是目前全球表现最好的电气化 ETF。业绩有起有落，没有保证。但供应链、资本开支（CAPEX）、利润池——

turns.en: perspective seems to be paying off. All right, Adam, one last question before we let you go here. What's next on your radar? What's blipping but kind of far out on the screen?
turns.zh: ——这套视角看来正在得到回报。好，Adam，在你离开之前最后一个问题。你雷达上接下来有什么？有什么还在屏幕边缘闪烁、离得尚远的东西？

turns.en: Oh, there's, look, AI is driving a lot of changes in a lot of different industries. I don't want to give any of my competitors any ideas, but there are quite a few industries where our bill of materials process really can work very well. So we've got them scoped out. We'll be dropping registration statements for them, you know, fairly soon. So, you know, that's the space we'll be active in. All right, nice little tease there from Adam Patty. Adam, thank you very much for
turns.zh: 哦，我是说，AI 正在推动很多不同行业的变化。我不想给竞争对手任何点子，但有相当多行业里，我们的物料清单流程真的能很好地起作用。我们已经把它们圈出来了，很快就会提交注册说明书。那就是我们接下来会活跃的领域。好——Adam 的一点小预告。Adam，非常感谢你——

turns.en: joining us here. We appreciate it. Come back and update us with those new ideas soon. All right. I will. Thank you, sir. All right. That's Adam Patty, the CEO of Vista Shares.
turns.zh: ——加入我们，我们很感激。有新想法的话，欢迎很快回来更新我们。——好的。谢谢你，先生。——以上是 Adam Padey，VistaShares 的 CEO。

turns.en: Thanks for listening. Join us again next week or head over to etfedge.cnbc.com. Over the last few decades, technology has transformed our world in amazing ways.
turns.zh: 谢谢收听。下周再见，或者访问 etfedge.cnbc.com。过去几十年间，科技以令人惊叹的方式改变了我们的世界。

turns.en: Through it all, Invesco QQQ ETF has connected investors to the forefront of innovation. Access the future today with Invesco QQQ. Let's rethink possibility. There are risks when investing in ETFs, including possible loss of money. ETF risks are similar to those of stocks.
turns.zh: 贯穿这一切，Invesco QQQ ETF 一直把投资者连接到创新的最前沿。现在就通过 Invesco QQQ 触达未来。Let's rethink possibility（重构无限可能）。投资 ETF 有风险，包括本金损失的可能。ETF 的风险与股票类似。

turns.en: Investments in the tech sector are subject to greater risk and more volatility than more diversified investments. The Nasdaq 100 index includes the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq. An investment cannot be made directly to an index.
turns.zh: 对科技板块的投资比更多元化的投资面临更大的风险和波动。纳斯达克 100 指数包含在纳斯达克上市的 100 家最大的非金融公司。投资者无法直接投资一个指数。

turns.en: Before investing, consider the fund's investment objectives, risks, charges and expenses. Visit Invesco.com for a prospectus containing this information. Read it carefully before investing. Invesco Distributors Inc.
turns.zh: 投资前，请考虑基金的投资目标、风险、费用与开销。请到 Invesco.com 获取包含这些信息的招募说明书，并在投资前仔细阅读。Invesco Distributors, Inc.
